name: Kedra Checkout Rules & Upsells
summary: Shopify app that hides, renames or reorders payment and shipping methods, validates the checkout and adds post-purchase upsells through no-code rules, with checkout analytics.
best_for: Shopify merchants who want to hide, rename or reorder payment and shipping methods, validate the checkout and add post-purchase upsells with rules instead of a developer, for a few dollars a month
skip_if: you need to add visual blocks or custom fields to the checkout page itself, which the app cannot do; or many of your orders are created as draft orders in the admin, where the rules do not apply
honest_knock: The free plan runs a single rule with a single condition, and Starter only three, and the listing and Kedra's own documentation disagree on whether that limit is per rule type or in total. The app cannot add anything visual to the checkout page, and rules skip draft orders made in the Shopify admin. We found no published refund or cancellation policy.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Starter · billed monthly through the Shopify invoice in USD
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-11-26 on the Shopify listing: prices, the 5 day trial and the $1 a month offer for the first 3 months unchanged; the 30% yearly saving checks out at about 30% on all three plans; Kedra's own docs still say 7 days) (Shopify App Store listing, read 15 Oct 2026 and read again 16 Nov 2026, prices in USD) Four plans, billed through your Shopify invoice. Free allows 1 active rule in total, of any type, with 1 condition per rule and 7 days of checkout analytics. Starter is $6.99 a month, or $58.70 a year, which the listing calls a 30% saving: 3 active rules in total, 3 conditions per rule and full checkout analytics. Starter Plus is $8.99 a month or $75.50 a year and adds post-purchase upsell offers. Unlimited is $12.99 a month or $109.10 a year, with unlimited checkout validation, payment and shipping, and shipping discount rules, and no limit on conditions per rule. Paid plans list a 5 day free trial (it said 7 days when we read it on 15 Oct 2026), and each paid plan lists $1 a month for the first 3 months (listing, read 16 Nov 2026). One inconsistency to know about: the listing counts the rule limit in total across all types, while Kedra's own pricing documentation describes it per rule type. The documentation also says stores that installed before 3 August 2026 keep unlimited rules.

Read on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-11-26.

free_plan_evidence: The free plan runs a single rule with a single condition, and Starter only three, and the listing and Kedra's own documentation disagree on whether that limit is per rule type or in total.

compare_with.name: Smarty Discounts
compare_with.why: Smarty Discounts is in our dossiers too and also works with rules in the Shopify checkout, but on the price side: tiered, capped and buy-X-get-Y discounts, with Lite at $9.99 a month or $99.99 a year when we read it on 11 October 2026. Kedra controls which payment and shipping options a shopper sees and whether the checkout goes through, from $6.99 a month. If your problem is the discount logic, look at Smarty Discounts; if it is the checkout options themselves, Kedra.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 16 November 2026 the session tested Kedra Checkout Rules and Upsells on the Free plan of a Shopify development store: a payment rule that did not work on the test gateway, a validation rule that blocked a 600 dollar test checkout, the Free plan limit, the plan screens up to the Shopify approval screen and the uninstall dialog. Nothing was paid or uninstalled. First rule: Manual Setup, the template Hide COD over an amount, edited into Hide Bogus gateway over USD 100 (order total greater than USD100, then hide payment methods that contain the string Bogus), saved ACTIVE at about 14:44:40. The Hide settings say that Credit card (Shopify Payments) can only be customized on Shopify Plus plans. A test checkout through the theme editor preview used a snowboard of 600 dollars, a made up name, address and email, and no card; nothing was paid. A first check before the rule existed (ski wax at 24.95 dollars) showed the card block Pay with credit card with a Testing instruction. The payment rule did not work: at 600 dollars Pay with credit card and Test Payment Gateway stayed visible, also after changing the string to Test Payment Gateway and then to Credit card. The cause was not established; it may be that the test gateway counts as the card block that is Plus only, but that is a guess. The Free plan allows 1 active rule: creating a second rule while one is active shows ACTIVE Locked with Your Free plan includes 1 active rule and it is in use. The payment rule was set to INACTIVE and a validation rule Block orders over an amount (order total greater than USD500, message Order total exceeds the maximum allowed amount.) was made ACTIVE. At about 14:49 a checkout of 600 dollars showed a red banner at the top that this order cannot be completed with the current checkout details. That is Shopify default text and not the app message; Your own checkout wording is not included on Free. A cart of 24.95 dollars showed no message. Timing, approximate tester observations: Install at 14:43:00 and a visibly working rule in the test checkout at 14:49:20, about 6 minutes 20 seconds, of which about 3 minutes went on the first rule that did not work; one working rule straight away would have taken about 2 minutes; more than 25 clicks and typing actions including the detour. Uninstall: the app menu offers Manage app, Get support, Pin to your navigation and Uninstall; the Uninstall dialog (reason list, feedback box) was opened and cancelled. Not tested: post-purchase upsells (a paid plan), hiding, renaming or reordering shipping and payment methods, draft orders, completing a real payment, Plus only features, own wording in the block, and a payment rule with a real second payment method. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The first rule, hiding the test payment method, did not work and cost about 3 minutes; the Free plan allows only 1 active rule, so the payment rule had to be made inactive before a validation rule could be active.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 16 November 2026 the session tested Kedra Checkout Rules and Upsells on the Free plan of a Shopify development store: a payment rule that did not work on the test gateway, a validation rule that blocked a 600 dollar test checkout, the Free plan limit, the plan screens up to the Shopify approval screen and the uninstall dialog. Nothing was paid or uninstalled. First rule: Manual Setup, the template Hide COD over an amount, edited into Hide Bogus gateway over USD 100 (order total greater than USD100, then hide payment methods that contain the string Bogus), saved ACTIVE at about 14:44:40. The Hide settings say that Credit card (Shopify Payments) can only be customized on Shopify Plus plans. A test checkout through the theme editor preview used a snowboard of 600 dollars, a made up name, address and email, and no card; nothing was paid. A first check before the rule existed (ski wax at 24.95 dollars) showed the card block Pay with credit card with a Testing instruction. The payment rule did not work: at 600 dollars Pay with credit card and Test Payment Gateway stayed visible, also after changing the string to Test Payment Gateway and then to Credit card. The cause was not established; it may be that the test gateway counts as the card block that is Plus only, but that is a guess. The Free plan allows 1 active rule: creating a second rule while one is active shows ACTIVE Locked with Your Free plan includes 1 active rule and it is in use. The payment rule was set to INACTIVE and a validation rule Block orders over an amount (order total greater than USD500, message Order total exceeds the maximum allowed amount.) was made ACTIVE. At about 14:49 a checkout of 600 dollars showed a red banner at the top that this order cannot be completed with the current checkout details. That is Shopify default text and not the app message; Your own checkout wording is not included on Free. A cart of 24.95 dollars showed no message. Timing, approximate tester observations: Install at 14:43:00 and a visibly working rule in the test checkout at 14:49:20, about 6 minutes 20 seconds, of which about 3 minutes went on the first rule that did not work; one working rule straight away would have taken about 2 minutes; more than 25 clicks and typing actions including the detour. Uninstall: the app menu offers Manage app, Get support, Pin to your navigation and Uninstall; the Uninstall dialog (reason list, feedback box) was opened and cancelled. Not tested: post-purchase upsells (a paid plan), hiding, renaming or reordering shipping and payment methods, draft orders, completing a real payment, Plus only features, own wording in the block, and a payment rule with a real second payment method. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The first rule, hiding the test payment method, did not work and cost about 3 minutes; the Free plan allows only 1 active rule, so the payment rule had to be made inactive before a validation rule could be active.
